title: Functions as arguments and results
description: Fold a range with any combiner, trace a composition, apply a function n times, count the calls a fixed-point search makes, then prepare a reading service within a budget.

learned: Pass a function where a rule is needed, not the value one call returned.
Read f(g(x)) inside out, and test order with functions that do not commute.
Return a function that keeps its settings and starts afresh on every call.
Count the calls a higher-order function makes by wrapping what you pass it.
recap.invariant: Before each step, the running result is the fold of term over exactly the points already visited.
recap.complexity: A fold over n points makes n calls each to term, next and combiner; repeated(f, n) makes n calls per use. Bounds assume constant-time callbacks and bounded-size numbers; drawing is excluded.
recap.common_mistake: Passing f(x) where f was meant, or reading f(g(x)) left to right.
in_real_programs: Python's sorted(items, key=f) takes the rule as an argument and calls it once per item.

retrieval.question: From your earlier Python: return or print — which hands a value back to the caller?
retrieval.answer: return hands the value back; print only writes text.
